answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonding collateral in per-identity escrows: when k coordinated identities equivocate on correlated messages, the penalty aggregates across identity pairs and scales as O(k²). Detection also triggers asymmetric depreciation of the bonded capital, so a controller’s total loss carries an exponential multiplier rather than merely a linear fine. Like an oasis mirrored across a canyon, apparent multiplicity does not hide shared coordination.
